nodes.summary: For classes $\mathfrak{F}$ and $\mathfrak{G}$ of finite groups, $\mathfrak{F} \subseteq \mathfrak{G}$ means that every finite group in $\mathfrak{F}$ belongs to $\mathfrak{G}$.
nodes.title: Inclusion of classes of finite groups

nodes.summary: For classes $\mathfrak F_1$ and $\mathfrak F_2$ of finite groups, their intersection $\mathfrak F_1 \cap \mathfrak F_2$ is the class of finite groups $G$ with $G \in \mathfrak F_1$ and $G \in \mathfrak F_2$. For formations $\mathfrak F_1$ and $\mathfrak F_2$ it is their meet in the lattice of formations.
nodes.title: Intersection of classes of finite groups

nodes.summary: A class of finite groups is a property of finite groups: for each finite group $G$ it states whether $G$ belongs to the class.
nodes.title: Class of finite groups (Kourovka 13.51)

nodes.summary: There is a finite modular lattice $L$ that admits no injective map $f$ from $L$ to the formations of finite groups such that, for all $a, b \in L$, $f(a \wedge b) = f(a) \cap f(b)$ and $f(a \vee b)$ is the smallest formation containing $f(a) \cup f(b)$. This answers Kourovka Problem 13.51 (Skiba) in the negative.
nodes.title: Not every finite modular lattice embeds in the lattice of formations

nodes.summary: For every finite modular lattice $L$ there is an injective map $f$ from $L$ to the formations of finite groups such that, for all $a, b \in L$, $f(a \wedge b) = f(a) \cap f(b)$ and $f(a \vee b)$ is the smallest formation containing $f(a) \cup f(b)$.
nodes.title: Kourovka Problem 13.51 (Skiba): finite modular lattices embed in the lattice of formations

nodes.summary: For classes $X$ and $Y$ of finite groups, the formation generated by $X \cup Y$ is the class of finite groups that belong to every formation containing both $X$ and $Y$. For formations $X$ and $Y$ it is their join in the lattice of formations.
nodes.title: Formation generated by two classes (Kourovka 10.56)

nodes.summary: For classes $\mathfrak F_1$ and $\mathfrak F_2$ of finite groups, their formation join is the class of finite groups $G$ that belong to every formation containing all groups of $\mathfrak F_1$ and of $\mathfrak F_2$: the intersection of all formations containing $\mathfrak F_1 \cup \mathfrak F_2$, which is the smallest such formation. For formations $\mathfrak F_1$ and $\mathfrak F_2$ it is their join in the…
nodes.title: Join of formations (Kourovka 13.51)

nodes.summary: A class of finite groups is given by its membership predicate: a proposition about each finite group, true exactly for the members of the class.
nodes.title: Classes of finite groups (Kourovka 10.56)

nodes.summary: A class of groups $\mathfrak{X}$ is given by a membership predicate on groups whose underlying type lies in the lowest universe, such that whenever a group $H$ belongs to $\mathfrak{X}$ and $K$ is a group isomorphic to $H$, the group $K$ also belongs to $\mathfrak{X}$.
nodes.title: Isomorphism-closed classes of groups (Kourovka 18.92)

nodes.summary: For classes of groups $\mathfrak{X}$ and $\mathfrak{Y}$, the class $\mathfrak{X}$ is included in $\mathfrak{Y}$, written $\mathfrak{X} \subseteq \mathfrak{Y}$, if every group that belongs to $\mathfrak{X}$ also belongs to $\mathfrak{Y}$.
nodes.title: Inclusion of group classes

nodes.summary: A set $\Theta$ of classes of groups is algebraic if every member $\mathfrak{A}$ of $\Theta$ is the join in $\Theta$ of some subset $S \subseteq \Theta$ all of whose members are compact in $\Theta$.
nodes.title: Algebraic sets of group classes

nodes.summary: Let $\Theta$ be a set of classes of groups and $\mathfrak{A}$ a class of groups. Then $\mathfrak{A}$ is compact in $\Theta$ if, for every subset $S \subseteq \Theta$ and every join $\mathfrak{J}$ of $S$ in $\Theta$ with $\mathfrak{A} \subseteq \mathfrak{J}$, there are a finite subset $S_1 \subseteq S$ and a join $\mathfrak{J}_1$ of $S_1$ in $\Theta$ with $\mathfrak{A} \subseteq \mathfrak{J}_1$.
nodes.title: Compact elements of a set of group classes

nodes.summary: A set $\Theta$ of classes of groups is a complete lattice of formations if it is nonempty, every member of $\Theta$ is a formation, for every nonempty subset $S \subseteq \Theta$ the intersection of the classes in $S$ (the class of groups belonging to every member of $S$) belongs to $\Theta$, and $\Theta$ has a member that contains every member of $\Theta$.
nodes.title: Complete lattices of formations

nodes.summary: A class $\mathfrak F$ of finite groups is a formation when it is closed under homomorphic images (if $G \in \mathfrak F$ and $\varphi : G \to H$ is a surjective homomorphism of finite groups, then $H \in \mathfrak F$) and, for every finite group $G$ and normal subgroups $N_1$ and $N_2$ of $G$, $G/N_1 \in \mathfrak F$ and $G/N_2 \in \mathfrak F$ imply $G/(N_1 \cap N_2) \in \mathfrak F$ (closure under finite…
nodes.title: Formation of finite groups (Kourovka 13.51)

nodes.summary: A class $X$ of finite groups is a formation if it is closed under isomorphism, contains the trivial group, contains $G/N$ whenever it contains $G$ and $N$ is a normal subgroup of $G$, and is closed under subdirect products: if $N_1$ and $N_2$ are normal subgroups of a finite group $G$ with $G/N_1 \in X$ and $G/N_2 \in X$, then $G/(N_1 \cap N_2) \in X$.
nodes.title: Formations of finite groups (Kourovka 10.56)

nodes.summary: A class $\mathfrak{X}$ of groups is a formation if every group in $\mathfrak{X}$ is finite, $\mathfrak{X}$ contains the trivial group, for every finite group $G$ in $\mathfrak{X}$ and every normal subgroup $N$ of $G$ the quotient $G/N$ lies in $\mathfrak{X}$, and for every finite group $G$ with normal subgroups $N_1$ and $N_2$ such that $G/N_1$ and $G/N_2$ lie in $\mathfrak{X}$, the quotient $G/(N_1 \cap N_2)$ lies…
nodes.title: Formations of finite groups (Kourovka 18.92)

nodes.summary: Let $\Theta$ and $S$ be sets of classes of groups. A class $\mathfrak{J}$ is the join of $S$ in $\Theta$ if $\mathfrak{J} \in \Theta$, every member of $S$ is contained in $\mathfrak{J}$, and $\mathfrak{J}$ is contained in every member of $\Theta$ that contains every member of $S$.
nodes.title: Joins in a set of group classes

nodes.summary: A class $\mathfrak{F}$ of finite groups is a local formation when it is a formation, contains the trivial group, and is saturated: a finite group $G$ belongs to $\mathfrak{F}$ whenever $G/\Phi(G)$ does, where $\Phi(G)$ is the Frattini subgroup of $G$.
nodes.title: Local formation of finite groups

nodes.summary: A set $\Theta$ of classes of groups is modular if for all $\mathfrak{A}, \mathfrak{B}, \mathfrak{C} \in \Theta$ with $\mathfrak{A} \subseteq \mathfrak{C}$ the following holds: whenever $\mathfrak{J}_1$ is the join in $\Theta$ of the set $\{\mathfrak{A}, \mathfrak{B} \cap \mathfrak{C}\}$ and $\mathfrak{D}$ is the join in $\Theta$ of the set $\{\mathfrak{A}, \mathfrak{B}\}$, the classes $\mathfrak{J}_1$ and…
nodes.title: Modular sets of group classes

nodes.summary: A class $X$ of finite groups is a formation of nilpotent groups of class at most $4$ if $X$ is a formation and every group $G$ in $X$ is nilpotent of class at most $4$, that is, the fourth term $\zeta_4(G)$ of the upper central series of $G$ is all of $G$.
nodes.title: Formations of nilpotent groups of class at most 4

nodes.summary: The meet of two classes $X$ and $Y$ of finite groups is their intersection $X \cap Y$: the class of finite groups that belong to both $X$ and $Y$.
nodes.title: Intersection of classes of finite groups (Kourovka 10.56)

nodes.summary: There exist formations $A$, $B$, $C$ of finite nilpotent groups of class at most $4$ such that the classes $A \cap (B \vee C)$ and $(A \cap B) \vee (A \cap C)$ differ, that is, some finite group lies in exactly one of them; here $X \vee Y$ denotes the formation generated by $X \cup Y$, the intersection of all formations containing $X$ and $Y$.
nodes.title: The lattice of nilpotent class-4 formations is not distributive (Kourovka 10.56)

nodes.summary: For all formations $A$, $B$, $C$ of finite nilpotent groups of class at most $4$, a finite group lies in $A \cap (B \vee C)$ if and only if it lies in $(A \cap B) \vee (A \cap C)$, where $X \vee Y$ denotes the formation generated by $X \cup Y$. That is, the lattice of formations of finite nilpotent groups of class at most $4$ is distributive (A. N. Skiba).
nodes.title: The distributivity question for nilpotent class-4 formations (Kourovka 10.56)

nodes.summary: There is a set $\Theta$ of classes of groups that is a complete lattice of formations of finite groups and is not algebraic; that is, Kourovka Problem 18.92(a) has a positive answer.
nodes.title: Non-algebraic complete lattices of formations exist

nodes.summary: The proposition that some set $\Theta$ of classes of groups is a complete lattice of formations of finite groups and is not algebraic.
nodes.title: Kourovka Problem 18.92(a) (A. N. Skiba)

nodes.summary: There is a complete lattice of formations of finite groups that is not modular: a nonempty set $\Theta$ of formations of finite groups, ordered by inclusion, that contains the intersection of each of its nonempty subsets and has a largest element, in which the modular law $A \vee (B \wedge C) = (A \vee B) \wedge C$ for $A \le C$ fails, joins being least upper bounds in $\Theta$ and meets intersections.
nodes.title: A non-modular complete lattice of formations exists (Kourovka 18.92(b))

nodes.summary: The proposition that there is a complete lattice of formations of finite groups that is not modular, joins being least upper bounds in the lattice and meets being intersections.
nodes.title: The non-modular formation lattice problem (Kourovka 18.92(b), A. N. Skiba)

nodes.summary: For a class $\mathfrak{F}$ of finite groups and a finite group $G$, the $\mathfrak{F}$-residual $G^{\mathfrak{F}}$ is the intersection of all normal subgroups $N$ of $G$ with $G/N \in \mathfrak{F}$.
nodes.title: Residual of a finite group with respect to a class

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
